messages:
maria: Hey—ran a 30s nsys capture on the 8xA100 node, load test with 1k concurrent streams. Timeline looks like kernels are tiny but we have big gaps where the host thread is idle and then a big HtoD memcpy serializes everything. posting screenshot and .qdrep soon :point_down:

jon: can you paste the nsys command and capture flags? curious if we traced os scheduling + cuda APIs

maria: ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --output=run1 ./svc_load_test --concurrency=1000`
attached the qdrep in /tmp (will upload). NVTXs show kvcache prefetch events before memcpy bursts.

lee: quick thought — are those memcpys using pageable buffers? if host memory isn't registered the copy engine will be synchronous-ish and stall kernels. also default stream interactions can serialize kernels if cudaMemcpy is used from the default stream.

sam: +1. also check whether we are using `cudaMemcpy` vs `cudaMemcpyAsync` on per-request path. The batcher sometimes falls back to synchronous copy when batch size is 1 (optim heuristic).

maria: looked at the trace: streams 3/4 run kernels, stream 0 does HtoD bursts. nsight shows the DMA engine overlaps with kernels but in our timeline the kernels wait for an event right after the memcpy, like `cudaStreamWaitEvent` is being used to synchronize. So overlap exists at HW level but logic introduces waits.

jon: can you grep for `cudaStreamWaitEvent` / host syncs in the trace? also check `pthread_kill`/sched_switch spikes — host preemptions could be delaying the thread that posts the event.

maria: yup — found repeated pattern: host thread posts async memcpy, then sleeps (~6-12ms) due to preemption, then posts event. GPU sits idle while DMA finished but kernel hasn't been launched. Snippet from nsys API trace: 
```
cudaMemcpyAsync(0x7f6a..., 0x7f7b..., 1.2MB, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream=1)
--- 2.1 ms --- (copy engine)
cudaEventRecord(..., stream=1)
(cudaStreamSynchronize?) <-- not directly called but we see cudaStreamWaitEvent on stream 0
... host sched_switch (sleep 9.3 ms) ...
cudaLaunchKernel(..., stream=1)
```
lee: interesting. So DMA completed but we didn't launch because host thread got preempted. That matches an OS-level scheduling gap. Check whether batcher/IO thread is pinned to a core or using thread pool that yields. If we have affinity churn, that could create ~10ms delays — visible as CPU wakeups in perf.

sam: another angle: are we using `cudaHostAlloc` with cudaHostAllocDefault or `cudaHostRegister` for the request buffers? If not, the driver may be staging and doing extra copies which can increase visible copy time and affect overlap semantics.

maria: we were not registering buffers. Code uses malloc + cudaMemcpyAsync. I'm seeing extra `memcpy` on host side in the trace (the app does a memcpy into a staging buffer right before cudaMemcpyAsync). So there's a 2-step host copy then the H2D. That host memcpy happens under a short mutex in the batcher and might be contending.

jon: That would explain the "tiny kernel, lots of host work" pattern — CPU-bound pre-copy, then DMA, then idle GPU while host gets preempted. Solutions: pre-register buffers or use pinned pool; move user memcpy outside critical path; or adopt zero-copy / GPUDirect if source is from network.

lee: also check batching heuristic: looks like we fallback to immediate single-request copies when batch size < threshold. Could we postpone submission until either batch full or a short micro-batch timer (e.g., 2ms) to avoid many 1-request memcpys? That reduces host bursts.

maria: tried emulating a 2ms micro-batch delay in the test harness. Result: throughput slightly up, tail latency reduced. Will run another nsys with host scheduling tracing.

perf-bot: advice: run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls,cupti_api --capture-range=cudaDriverApi` and include `--sample=cpu` to see user-space samples. For perfetto-style flame use `nsys export --format=chrome_tracing`.

sam: another interesting data point — KV cache prefetch currently runs in the same IO thread; it prefetches kvs for the next batch and does a few `memmove`/memcpy ops. If prefetch is moved to a dedicated pinned thread with SCHED_FIFO low prio or a thread pinned to a core, we might avoid being preempted mid-sequence.

maria: full plan: 1) switch staging buffers to cudaHostAlloc/pinned pool; 2) separate prefetch into dedicated thread pinned to core; 3) avoid cudaStreamWaitEvent between copy and launch if possible (use event recorded in same stream); 4) adjust micro-batching timer. I'll run three nsys captures (baseline, pinned buffers, pinned thread) and post results.

jon: small probe: instrument where `cudaStreamWaitEvent` is inserted — maybe our rollout/backout logic uses cross-stream sync to ensure ordering across batchers. If it's intentional we need to gate it behind capacity/quantile config.

lee: and if you see the copy engine overlapping with kernels in hw but still serialization in trace, it's usually host-side ordering or stream interop with default stream. Also confirm driver version; older drivers have pathological default stream semantics.

maria: noted driver is 470.161.03 on test node. I'll test on 520.x as well. thanks all, uploading qdrep + json exports in ~30m. :rocket:

jon: thanks — ping when uploads are up, I'll run the same probe with perf and schedstat to get wakeup latencies.

sam: nice triage. if we confirm preemption, we should add a unit check in CI that runs a tiny capture and asserts host-side scheduling gaps < 5ms under baseline load.

maria: agreed. will follow up with captures and a short doc of changes.
